column2: Ill tidings. The fleet that sailed into the mists off Albion has drifted back to open water with every sail still set and not a soul aboard. [albion_lost_commander.GetTitledFirstName] was found alone at the helm, speaking of grey shapes in the fog and a voice that sang from the stones. The rest of the host is simply gone.\n\nThe Mists of Albion swallow any army that sails into them. The tribes of Albion and the Fimir know the way through the outer mists, and a guide, a Truthsayer or a Dark Emissary, may lead others through (decision: Seek a Guide through the Mists). Nobody passes the innermost mist.
I will be more careful.
Do not warn me of this again.
The Mists of Albion

News has come from the captains of the western sea: the mists off the coast of Norsca have thinned and broken, and where there was only fog there is now an island. Its people call it Albion. It is a land of bog and fen, of hill forts and giants' bones, and of great standing stones carved with signs older than the elves. Its tribes are fierce, the Fimir lurk in its fens, and some say the stones were raised by the Old Ones themselves. Whatever kept Albion hidden has failed, and every power of the Old World will want what lies there.\n\nAlbion can now be invaded with most casus belli, and its people can be married.

The mists are gone. For as long as the tribes remember, the grey veil kept the sea-wolves of Norsca and the iron men of the east away from Albion. Now, from the cliffs, the sails of the outsiders can be seen on the horizon. The Truthsayers say the Ogham stones have failed, as the Old Ones warned they would when the Dark Masters grew strong. The tribes must hold Albion with spears instead of fog.\n\nAlbion can now be invaded with most casus belli, and its people can be married.

The veil is torn. The Ogham stones that wove the mists are failing, and the power the Old Ones bound in Albion lies open to whoever is strong enough to take it. The Dark Emissaries rejoice. Soon the hosts of the Old World will come to fight over the stones, and the fens will run red, and the Dark Masters will drink it all.\n\nAlbion can now be invaded with most casus belli, and its people can be married.
Then we will hold it with spears.
Let them come, and let the stones fall.
A new land, and old secrets.

A grey-robed seer came ashore at dawn, on a fishing boat no harbour master saw arrive. The stranger is a Truthsayer of Albion, a keeper of the Ogham stones that the Old Ones raised to bind the island's power. The servants of the Dark Masters are gathering on Albion, the Truthsayer says, and the stones need defenders: your fleets will be led through the outer mists. There is one price beyond your gold. You must swear on the stones never to defile them. Break that oath, and the mists will remember.

A stranger in a cloak of black feathers came aboard one of your ships in the night and was found sitting at the captain's table at dawn. The stranger is a Dark Emissary of Albion, a Truthsayer who turned to the Dark Masters, and will lead your fleets through the outer mists, for the Dark Masters want the Ogham stones toppled and need strong arms to do it. The Emissary has taken your price, but asks for one thing more: a life, given to the fens.
I swear it, on the stones.
I swear no oaths to hedge-seers.
Take one of my prisoners.
Take one of my own warriors.

Your agents found a guide on the northern coasts: a ragged fisherman who swore he knew the paths through the mists, and who was paid in advance. He was last seen rowing west into the fog. Whether he was a fraud or the mists took him, the price is gone.
Curse him. I will find another.

The Ogham stone at [albion_stone.GetName] has fallen. Your warriors hauled it down with ropes and chains while the Dark Emissaries chanted, and when it struck the earth the ground shook and the mist that hung over the place thinned to nothing. [Root.albion_dark_stones.GetValue] of Albion's great stones now stand dark. When six are dark, it is said, the mists will fail entirely.
Let the next one fall.
The sixth stone is dark: the Mists of Albion will fail.

The Ogham stone at [albion_stone.GetName] stands again. The Truthsayers sang over it for three nights, scouring the marks of the Dark Masters from its face, and on the fourth morning the mist rose from the earth around it once more. [Root.albion_dark_stones.GetValue] of Albion's great stones still stand dark.
The stones endure.

Word has come from [albion_stone.GetName]: the Ogham stone there has been toppled by [From.GetTitledName] and the servants of the Dark Masters. The Truthsayers say that [Root.albion_dark_stones.GetValue] of the great stones now stand dark. At six the mists will fail, and Albion will lie open to the world.
[From.GetFirstName] will answer for this.

The Truthsayer's warning has come true. Since the stone fell, your sleep has been full of grey fog and a voice that sings from the stones, and you wake cold and weak. The mists will no longer part for your ships. You swore an oath on the stones, and you broke it.
It is only a dream.

A ship has drifted onto your coast out of the fog. Its sails are whole and its holds are full, and there is not a soul aboard: another outsider who sailed into the mists without a guide. The fishermen will not go near it, but the cargo is there for the taking.
Strip it bare.
Burn it on the shore, an offering to the stones.
Sink it in the fens for the Dark Masters.
Seek a Guide through the Mists

The Mists of Albion swallow any army that sails into them. Send word to the fishing villages of the northern coasts for someone who knows the paths: a Truthsayer of Albion or, for those who serve the Dark Masters, a Dark Emissary. A guide will lead your fleets through the outer mists for five years, though not through the innermost one. Some guides are frauds. Costs 100 gold, or 300 prestige for a chief or a boss.
Guided through the Mists
A guide of Albion leads this lord's fleets through the outer Mists of Albion.
Blood Price
One of this lord's own warriors was given to a Dark Emissary, and the men talk of it.
Truthsayer's Curse
This lord broke an oath sworn on the Ogham stones. The mists remember.
Toppled an Ogham stone
